newsitem.title: USA: ADM sees its ethanol market share dropping.
newsitem.headline: ADM sees its ethanol market share dropping.

text.p: Leading ethanol producer Archer Daniels Midland Co expects its share of the U.S. ethanol market to fall another five percentage points this year as it diversifies into non-fuel alcohols, an ADM executive said.
"Our market share is down to 40 percent and we will be down by the end of the year to 35 percent," ADM senior vice president Martin Andreas told Reuters at an ethanol conference here.
"Our decline is on purpose. We want more diversification. We are adding refining flexibility with the addition of beverage alcohol and industrial alcohol," Andreas said.

Andreas declined to give production figures for ADM but said part of the company's decline in market s "Our decline is on purpose. We want more diversification. We are adding refining flexibility with the addition of beverage alcohol and industrial alcohol," Andreas said.
Andreas declined to give production figures for ADM but said part of the company's decline in market share was due to additional plants that have been added in the industry.

ADM and other producers last year cut back ethanol production as corn prices soared to record highs, but output has been gradually recovering. Total U.S. production capacity is about 1.6 billion gallons a year.
